# Preparation Plan

Builds a preparation clause’s connection contracts and initial state, adding process refresh, optional party admission, document-access registration and source-pattern validators. `plan` returns these definitions; producing a plan does not itself install them or confirm a process outcome. Executable configuration remains literal data during planning.

## Configuration and connections

`clauseKey` selects `/clauseRuntime/work/candidate/<clauseKey>`. Paths refer to the document where the corresponding computation executes.

- Clause `bindings` override `type/defaultBindings`. Property bindings must satisfy `type/bindingTypes`; omission is allowed for names in `type/optionalBindings`. A `pointer` binding must be text beginning with `/` and cannot be `/` alone. Bindings must name declared properties, actions or `childActions`.
- Actions come from `type/actions`, or `parameters/actions` when `type/configurableActions` is true. Absent actions are permitted when `type/initialState` supplies an object. Each structural initial value must be an object associated with a named pointer binding. `parameters/conditions` may reference only known actions.
- Clause, action and connection names must be nonempty text without `.`, `/` or `~`. Action bindings are dictionaries of named connections. An action’s `automatic` connection is inserted as `_automatic`; a supplied connection cannot occupy that name when the action defines it. `automatic.pathBinding` resolves through property bindings.
- `snapshotBindings` capture existing document values through text paths; missing values are rejected. Generated `parameters` normally capture clause parameters excluding `actions` and `conditions`; `readParametersFromDocument: true` instead makes that constant `{}`. `actionDefinition` supplies the shared action implementation.

Each connection’s `on` selects `event`, `initialized` (`Clauses Initialized`), `activated` (`Document Activated`), `change`, `embedded`, `collection`, `channel`, `workflow` or `timer`. Unsupported fields are rejected. `change`, `embedded` and `collection` require a non-root `path`; collection handling filters for descendants of that path. `event` supplies a matching pattern. `channel` names an existing channel. `workflow` creates a callable operation using `party`, or otherwise `channel`, and can carry a `request` definition. This wiring does not establish a particular person’s authority or obligation.

`embedded` and `collection` sources contribute their paths for embedding unless `embed` is false. Explicit `embeds` and `embedsCollections` must identify declared pointer bindings.

## Generated execution and state

Connections merge action `defaults` with connection `params`, with connection values taking precedence. `when` defaults to true; a false result skips execution. Action `args` are checked when declared. `require/when` and the action’s `parameters/conditions` entry also default to true, but false results reject execution. The default requirement error is `ACTION_REQUIREMENT_FAILED`.

Execution proceeds through action `preflight`, connection `before`, action `do`, then connection `after`. A supplied preflight must set `actionResult.outcome` to `acceptedNew`, `duplicate`, `rejected` or `skipped`; only `acceptedNew` continues. `resultContract: "outcome-v1"` applies the same outcome requirement after `do`, and only `acceptedNew` reaches `after`. The default `resultContract` is `legacy`, which does not enforce that result check. An accepted action result does not by itself confirm an external outcome.

`/connectionState_<clauseKey>/<actionName>.<connectionName>` initially contains `armed: false` and `fired: false`. `once` defaults to false and must be Boolean. When true, execution skips an already-fired connection and marks `fired` only after reaching the end of its generated body. These flags describe connection handling, not business completion; missing runtime values do not establish their planned defaults.

## Timers

A timer requires exactly one of `timestamp` and `afterEvent`:

- `timestamp` is an integer Unix deadline in microseconds, from 0 through 9007199254740991. Absolute timers arm on clause initialization and reject `delayMs` or `policy`.
- `afterEvent` identifies the arming source. `delayMs` is a positive integer in milliseconds, at most 9007199254740, measured from that source’s logical timestamp. The resulting deadline must remain within the timestamp range. `policy` defaults to `first`; `latest` replaces the pending keyed request on subsequent eligible triggers.

`afterEvent` and optional `cancelOn` use `event`, `change`, `channel`, `embedded`, `collection` or `initialized` selectors, but `afterEvent` cannot use initialization because it has no timestamp. A supplied `cancelOn` cannot be empty.

Arming sets `armed` and emits a Timer Request with key `connection`, capturing the trigger and source path. `first` suppresses subsequent arming once `armed` is true; neither cancellation nor firing clears that flag in this plan. `once` also prevents rearming after `fired` becomes true. Cancellation emits a Cancel Timer Request and cannot undo an earlier firing.

Only committed requests affect timer registrations. Firing requires the supported Time runtime, a valid pending registration and complete input-history evidence; processing may occur after the logical deadline. New deadlines must follow the invocation’s causal timestamp, except that a new standalone initialization without a prior causal position may request an already-elapsed deadline. `armed` is not proof that a timer remains pending or has fired.

## Process refresh and admission

`/process_<clauseKey>` is planned with `entries: {}`. The refresh destination is taken directly from the clause’s `bindings`, using the name in `type/destinationBinding`. Destination updates and an Embedded Node Channel without a `sourcePath` filter each invoke `sharedRefresh` from `actionDefinition`.

Admission configuration comes from `/clauseRuntime/work/candidate/activation/parameters/admission/approvers`, defaulting to `[]`. An empty list adds no admission state or operations. Otherwise every approver must be a distinct key in activation `parameters/parties`; violations reject planning with `ADMISSION_APPROVER_NOT_A_PARTY` or `ADMISSION_DUPLICATE_APPROVER`.

Admission initializes `/process_<clauseKey>/admission` with `editable: true`, empty `grants` and `retired`, and a `ledger` containing `revision: 1`, `proposal: {}` and `history: {}`. The amendment bindings point `state` to this ledger and `editable` to its sibling flag; only the `grants` path is amendable.

Updates to `/activation` or the process state run the admission workflow. A ready `nextAdmissionRequest` is recorded as a proposal. A ready `admissionInstallRequest` leads to `admitApprovedParties` followed by `finishAdmission`. The process-entry schema and the detailed refresh, installation and rebase rules depend on the supplied action implementation and activation runtime; the plan alone does not establish their outcomes.

Proposal recording requires the current `expectedRevision`, the permitted `path`, `editable: true`, and a nonempty `proposalId` without `/` or `~`. An identical pending proposal is a duplicate; conflicting reuse or reuse of a historical identifier is rejected. `preservePending` defaults to false; true rejects replacement of a different pending proposal. A new proposal records its exact `replacement`, resets approvals and emits an event with `kind: "Amendment Proposed"`.

Each approver receives `approveAdmission_<clauseKey>_<role>`, accepting `proposalId`. It requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion: true`, otherwise `EXACT_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, and the calling channel must be a configured approver. Already-applied identifiers return `duplicate`; otherwise the identifier must match the pending proposal and `editable` must still be true, including for repeated pending approvals. Only unanimous approval replaces `grants`, records the identifier in `history`, increments `revision`, clears `proposal` and emits `kind: "Amendment Applied"`. Recording one approval does not establish admission completion.

Each approver also receives `rebaseAdmission_<clauseKey>_<role>`, passing `admissionRef` and optional preparation entry `key` to `rebaseAdmissionPublic`. `key` defaults to `single` for a singleton preparation.

## Document access and source validation

Each configured party receives `registerAccess_<clauseKey>_<role>`. Its `documents` request contains 1–16 existing initialized Timeline Access publications, whose required permission fields are `allowedTimelines` and `allowedKeys`. The registration contract calls for initialization, authority and permitted-access verification through `registerDocumentAccessPublic`, then invokes activation `refresh`. It passes `/processAccess_<clauseKey>` as `basePath` and adds that path to embedded `collectionPaths`; registration is not itself confirmation of admission or newly granted access.

For generated steps containing `connectionConfiguration`, source declarations come from `parameters/template`, falling back to the captured `template` snapshot. Template `sources` and each clause’s `parameters/sources` are combined, treating omitted declaration maps as empty. Unequal declarations under the same alias reject planning with `SOURCE_DECLARATION_CONFLICT`. The generated `configuredSources` returns the combined declarations; `sourceDeclarationMatches` checks the supplied source against its alias’s pattern and returns false for unknown aliases.

`validateConfiguration` returns `allowed: true` with an empty `code`; planning still performs the checks above. `validateTransition` always returns `allowed: false` with `PREPARATION_IMMUTABLE_WHILE_OBLIGATIONS_EXIST`. Despite that code’s wording, this function does not inspect whether obligations exist.
